books.section: Topic 5.8 Military Conflict in the Civil War
Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

primary_sources: Abraham Lincoln, letter to Horace Greeley (August 22, 1862)

stimulus.source_note: Abraham Lincoln, letter to Horace Greeley, August 22, 1862. Public domain; quoted as printed in Princeton Review, Chapter 9 supplement. “. . .” marks omitted text.
stimulus.text:
“If I could save the Union without freeing any slave I would do it, and if I could save it by freeing all the slaves I would do it; and if I could save it by freeing some and leaving others alone I would also do that. What I do about slavery, and the colored race, I do because I believe it helps to save the Union. . . .”

—Abraham Lincoln, letter to Horace Greeley, August 22, 1862

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note

rationales.A: Lincoln names saving the Union as the goal; emancipation is judged by whether it helps that goal.
rationales.B: Lincoln says he would free all, some, or none, depending on what saves the Union.
rationales.C: Lincoln weighs every course by one test: does it help to save the Union.
rationales.D: Lincoln is writing to Greeley, not promising anything to the South.
rationales.general:
1. Lincoln lists three courses: free none, free all, free some and leave others.
2. He says he would take whichever one saves the Union.
3. The test is not what is most just in the abstract; it is what saves the Union.
4. Emancipation is a tool in the sentence, and the Union is the purpose.
Remember: when a leader lists three options and one test, the test is the goal.
